questions.question: You cannot pass a school bus when its red lights are flashing.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: When you see a school bus with flashing red lights, you must stop before reaching it. Stay stopped until the lights turn off. On a road with a median, vehicles on the opposite side do not need to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and prepare to stop if cars are approaching.
Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
Go carefully through the intersection without always stopping.
Stop only for traffic on a crossing road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A stop sign means you must come to a complete stop. Let other cars and pedestrians go first. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When driving near a truck, remember that trucks generally:

options.text: Need more distance to stop than smaller cars.
Need less time to pass going downhill than smaller cars.
Need a smaller turning space than smaller cars.
Need less time to pass going uphill than smaller cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need more distance to stop than smaller cars.
questions.explanation: Because of their size, trucks take longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.

questions.question: You notice the driver ahead is driving with one hand and talking to a passenger. You should:

options.text: Give that vehicle extra space.
Realize that driver is distracted and less safe.
Do not copy that driver's behavior.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted while driving. If another driver seems distracted, stay farther away from them because they are more likely to have an accident.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, you should:

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and roll down your window.
Have your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
Get out and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel and ask passengers to keep their hands visible. Stay in your car unless the officer tells you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your license, registration, and insurance.

questions.question: Seat belts work best when worn by:

options.text: Only the driver.
Passengers on long trips.
Everyone on expressways.
Everyone every time the car is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: Everyone every time the car is driven.
questions.explanation: All passengers must wear seat belts every time you drive. Without a seat belt, a person can become a projectile and hurt others in the car during a crash.

questions.question: Driving ability can be harmed by:

options.text: Alcohol.
Any medication.
Not enough sleep.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Safe driving depends on being in good health. Alcohol, drugs, and being tired can all harm your ability to drive.

questions.question: A seat belt should be adjusted so that it:

options.text: Is loose.
Fits snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Is hidden under the seat.
Stops the seat belt alarm from going off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should rest comfortably so you can fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot when:

options.text: Pulling toward or away from a curb.
Turning left or right.
Changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot every time you move your car. Check before turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: To change lanes you should:

options.text: Check mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you want to move, then change lanes.
Signal, check mirrors, and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you want to move, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal first. Check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure no one else is moving into that lane. Change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: It starts to sleet or snow while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Stay farther back from the vehicle in front of you.
Be careful around all other vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: In snow, keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Increase the distance between your car and the car in front of you. Wet, cold roads are slippery and take longer to stop on.

questions.question: Another driver cuts you off in traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Pull next to the driver and yell at them.
Let it go.
Flash your high beams at the driver.
Cut them off to get back at them.

questions.explanation: Do not take it personally if another driver cuts you off. Let it go and keep driving safely. This prevents road rage and accidents.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding can kill.
Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.
Both A and B are true.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B are true.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash. At speeds above 80 miles per hour, survival is almost impossible. Driving much slower than other traffic is also dangerous because other drivers may make risky moves to pass you.

questions.question: You missed your exit on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Go to the next exit.
Make a U-turn across the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.
Flag down a police officer to escort you back.

questions.explanation: Take the next exit. Do not stop, back up, or cross lanes suddenly on the highway. Do not turn around across the median. These actions are illegal and very dangerous.

questions.question: When should you always use your turn signal?

options.text: When changing lanes.
When pulling into or out of a parking space.
When pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signal whenever you move left or right. Signal when leaving a parking space, changing lanes, or entering traffic.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is coming toward you with flashing red or blue lights. What should you do?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before it catches up.
Keep driving but stay out of its way.
Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles with sirens and flashing lights pass. Pull to the right edge of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull over.

questions.question: In a funeral procession, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: Another driver
A pedestrian
The funeral procession
A bicyclist

questions.explanation: Drivers, pedestrians, and bicyclists must yield to funeral processions. When the first vehicle enters an intersection, the other vehicles can follow through, even if the traffic light is red.

questions.question: What happens if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the alcohol's effect.
The alcohol helps the medicine work better.
The effects of both can be much stronger together.
There is no effect because they are different.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of both can be much stronger together.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with medicine can increase how much both affect you. One drink combined with cold medicine could feel like multiple drinks without the medicine.

questions.question: How should you safely cross railroad tracks?

options.text: Look both ways, but only when the red light is flashing.
Listen and look both ways, then cross if it is safe.
Cross quickly when a train is approaching.
Quickly pass under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen and look both ways, then cross if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Always look and listen for trains from both directions before crossing. Watch for warning signals. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: What will help someone who has drunk alcohol feel better?

options.text: Tomato juice and lime
Hot coffee
Fresh air
Only time

questions.explanation: Only time will allow the body to get over the effects of alcohol.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with no warning signals, should a driver slow down, look, and listen?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: If there are no warning devices or only a crossbuck sign, slow down. Look both ways at the tracks and listen for a train. Only cross when it is safe.

questions.question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When a flagger directs you to stop.
When there is a stop sign.
When flashing red signals and gates are operating.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to, when a stop sign is present, or when flashing red signals and gates are operating.

questions.question: Which statement is true about seat belts and child restraints?

options.text: Never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
Airbags can hurt an infant or small child, even in a low-speed crash.
All passengers must use a seat belt or child restraint.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce the chance of injury or death in a crash. Children 12 and under should sit in a rear seat with proper restraints. Never put a rear-facing infant seat in the front of a vehicle with a front airbag.

questions.question: The most common mistake when backing is not looking both ways behind the vehicle.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: The most common backing mistake is not looking both ways behind you. Mirrors do not show everything. Turn your body and head to the right and look through the rear window.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately.
Help injured people.
Call the police.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop right away. If possible, move your vehicle out of traffic. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Do not move injured people unless necessary. Apply direct pressure to stop heavy bleeding. Wait for emergency vehicles.

questions.question: What does alcohol do to a driver?

options.text: Slows reflexes and reaction time.
Puts you to sleep.
Wakes you up.
Improves your judgment.

questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant that slows your brain and reduces your driving skills. It slows reaction time and impairs judgment.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn.
No stopping.
No U-turn.
Detour ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: A "Merging lanes" sign means you should be ready to change lanes or let other traffic in.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: A "Merging lanes" sign means two lanes going the same direction will soon join into one. Be ready to change lanes or let other traffic merge in.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to whom?

options.text: Vehicles in the roundabout.
Bicyclists in the roundabout.
Pedestrians in the roundabout.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: Signaling before turning, changing lanes, or leaving a curb is:

options.text: Only needed if other traffic is nearby.
A good habit and required by law.
Only needed during the maneuver, not before.
Not needed if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: A good habit and required by law.
questions.explanation: Signal your intentions before turning or changing lanes. The law requires you to signal at least 100 feet before moving left or right. Always signal before pulling away from a curb.
